provenance: Official JavaScript renderer README, MIT license, package metadata, renderVisitor and package synchronization implementation inspected at commit 2d3897cc92cca191db7f7cea852b90b6f332045a.
discoveries: The renderer generates typed JavaScript client codecs for accounts, instructions, PDAs, events, errors and program IDs from Codama IDLs; these clients target @solana/kit, while SYLPH currently uses web3.js v1.
For Node ESM/TypeScript NodeNext it supports explicit .js import extensions, while dependency and link overrides are emitted verbatim and therefore require caller validation.
The visitor deletes the generated directory by default and synchronizes or creates package.json dependencies by default; generation must be isolated and its package mutations reviewed.

default generation can delete output files and mutate package.json
renderer targets @solana/kit; import overrides and module format can be incompatible with current SYLPH build
validation: pin IDL, renderer, visitor and transitive dependency versions
generate only in an isolated temporary package and review every file and manifest diff
compare generated bytes and decode behavior against official SDK and confirmed transaction/account fixtures; reject unknown discriminators

provenance: Official Anza wincode README, workspace/package manifests, license and fuzz harness inspected at commit a00f1d73caf2a1024dd81d0822285587de447a1c.

The README cites independent reviews for release 0.1.2, whereas the pinned package is 0.6.3; the older audit statement does not certify the current version.

risks: bincode compatibility is not universal across schema, config, version, integer and enum choices
current 0.6.3 code is newer than the 0.1.2 audit release cited by the README
placement initialization uses unsafe Rust internals and requires version-specific review
validation: generate fixtures with the pinned Agave/bincode schema and compare every relevant byte sequence
test truncation, invalid enum tags, lengths, integer bounds and configuration changes

provenance: Official deBridge serializer README, package metadata/license, ExternalInstruction Rust specification and Solidity test fixtures inspected at commit 71dc19675996ab6c5b537a3072c2386aaff45fe4.
discoveries: This Solidity library serializes deBridge ExternalInstruction payloads for EVM-to-Solana cross-chain calls; the documented target layout corresponds to a Rust serde/bincode struct.
Its tests compare several Solidity serialization helpers with explicit byte arrays for pubkey substitutions, seed variants, data substitutions and instruction account metadata.

The package is LGPL-3.0-only and explicitly assigns callers responsibility for preparing correct values; correct byte packaging does not establish safe destination-program behavior or bridge authorization.

EVM-to-Solana encoding errors can redirect accounts or change amounts and authorization fields
serializer correctness cannot validate bridge message authenticity or destination instruction effects
validation: keep out of scope unless the product adds an explicitly reviewed cross-chain feature
if relevant, pin deBridge protocol version and compare full payload bytes to official Rust-generated fixtures

provenance: Official Firedancer solana_dissector README, GPL-2.0 license and Lua protocol dissector inspected at commit 1341a3a3d25d14dc9313c1ec2a9f5478abcde934.
discoveries: The Wireshark Lua plugin decodes portions of Solana gossip, shred and repair traffic using hard-coded port mappings; the README says gossip port mappings are not implemented and may require manual Decode As.

provenance: Official Codama Spec README, MIT package metadata, v1 spec/schema artifacts and contribution conventions inspected at commit ef6742ddc3d14915aa799e809d9ceb92c39a829e.
discoveries: The repository defines a versioned typed-node specification; the inspected npm package is 1.9.2 while the public Codama spec constant shown in the README is 1.8.0, so package version and schema version must not be conflated.

The checked-in v1/schema.json is explicitly a generated placeholder/stub, so it cannot be treated as a complete JSON Schema validator for Codama IDLs.

risks: package and spec versions are separate and can evolve independently

the checked-in JSON Schema is a stub and will not provide complete structural validation
validation: pin the published @codama/spec package and spec version separately
validate real IDLs with the pinned reference validator instead of the placeholder schema
test absent/empty arrays, optional fields, declaration ordering and generated codec bytes

provenance: Official Rust parser SDK README, MIT license, Cargo manifest, Yellowstone event queue, ordered buffers, dropped-event metrics and parser modules inspected at commit 1a21a76352055589e62aaa4b8b3376dfcefb4a21. No build, benchmark, live feed or test suite was run.
discoveries: The v0.7.13 Rust library advertises Pump/PumpSwap, LaunchLab, Raydium, Meteora and Orca parsers across Yellowstone, ShredStream, RPC and account sources, with default Borsh and opt-in zero-copy parser backends; its Cargo manifest requires Rust 1.91 and pins Agave/Solana crate versions.

The Yellowstone client uses a bounded ArrayQueue; when full it increments dropped-event counters and emits rate-limited warnings rather than preserving the event. Ordered buffers also drop late data with an explicit continuity-break warning, and the README states ordering cannot guarantee upstream completeness.

The README reports microsecond parsing and other performance improvements, but those are upstream claims; this review did not reproduce them, and fast parser output remains dependent on source completeness, protocol fixtures and commitment.
patterns: make queue overflow countable and operator-visible, but treat any drop as an integrity failure for canonical observations
separate parser CPU backend from input provenance and preserve source/slot/transaction identity
when ordering buffers drop late records, emit a continuity incident and require independent replay/reconciliation
sources.overlap: Substantial parser and stream overlap with SYLPH. Its queue/drop counters and explicit ordering warnings are useful audit references, but introducing a second Rust DEX parser would duplicate Truth-X and create another protocol-truth boundary. SYLPH already fails closed on live queue overflow; preserve that behavior.
risks: zero-copy backend and Rust 1.91/Agave 4.2 dependency surface need independent memory-safety and compatibility review
upstream benchmark claims are not independently reproduced and do not measure canonical completeness or transaction landing
ShredStream and non-finalized streams can be incomplete/reorganized; an ordered parser cannot certify upstream coverage
validation: differentially parse pinned confirmed/finalized transactions for every protocol and parser backend
inject a full queue, late slot, duplicate transaction, parser failure and reconnect gap; assert counters and continuity incidents

provenance: Official Node SDK README, MIT package metadata, Yellowstone client implementation, ShredStream documented limitations and queue metrics inspected at commit dfdb0e07d38c7611326e5ccf23617c6b9111fd4c. No package installation, build, test, live stream or replay was executed.
discoveries: The v0.5.19 Node SDK wraps a Rust N-API Yellowstone transport and DEX parser; it documents a bounded pre-parser ingress queue, async-iterator output and separate ingress/public-event drop counters. Its default queue overflow behavior is drop-newest, so observability does not itself prevent loss.

On reconnect it requests `fromSlot` at the last parsed slot, keeps a bounded deduplication window (128 slots by default), and increments continuity-break status when replay is rejected/disabled; provider acceptance does not prove a complete retained replay.

Its ShredStream Pump example explicitly skips and counts cold ALT-cache misses without replaying them, requiring tables to be prewarmed; this is a deliberate incompleteness signal, not a complete transaction view.
patterns: report ingress drops separately from consumer-queue drops and make both visible to the operator
resume inclusively from the last fully parsed point, deduplicate replay, and mark continuity unknown when the provider rejects replay
count skipped ALT/cache-dependent events and keep them out of complete/canonical datasets until recovered
sources.overlap: Direct overlap with SYLPH feed, parser and replay code. These are comparison patterns rather than an adoption recommendation: the SDK’s default queue drop policy would be unsafe as a replacement for SYLPH’s live overflow fault latch, and its replay cursor is not a contiguous-chain certificate.
risks: drop-newest queue policy can lose observations even while the stream remains connected
provider `fromSlot` support/retention is not guaranteed; a bounded replay dedupe window cannot establish complete history
N-API/native transport and SDK version alignment add platform and supply-chain constraints; README requires Node >=20.18
validation: inject ingress and public queue overflow independently and assert drop counters, continuity state and caller-visible errors
test reconnect from last parsed slot with duplicates, unsupported fromSlot, no replay data and provider retention gaps
test cold ALT cache misses remain explicitly incomplete until authoritative lookup/replay repairs them

provenance: Official solana-dex-parser README, MIT package metadata/license, protocol dispatch map, transaction adapter and parse error handling inspected at commit 0c67d8ffa78c7fb2e80230ec53d0627c9531566a. No package installation, build or test suite was run.
discoveries: The v2.6.7 TypeScript package dispatches trade/liquidity/meme-event parsers by explicit program ID and consumes both outer and inner instructions; its adapter resolves v0 loaded writable/readonly addresses when transaction metadata includes them.

It exposes transaction status, compute units, signer, SOL/token balance changes and `meta.fee`; the `fee` field is the transaction metadata fee in lamports and does not by itself decompose priority fees, tips, protocol fees or realized net trade cost.

Parser exceptions become `state=false` and a message unless `throwError` is enabled, while an unrecognized transaction can return an otherwise successful empty result; callers must distinguish “no recognized event” from a validated no-op.
patterns: normalize multi-hop protocol dispatch while retaining original program, instruction and inner-instruction provenance
use transaction metadata and pre/post balances as independent reconciliation fields alongside parsed swap legs
expose parse failure state explicitly and distinguish unknown/no-match from a successfully validated empty result
sources.overlap: Offers another TypeScript DEX parser across Jupiter, Pump, Raydium, Meteora and Orca, overlapping with SYLPH Truth-X and its execution/accounting path. Its fee and swap outputs may be useful for offline differential fixtures only, not as net PnL or quote authority.
risks: program support claims do not prove current discriminator/layout parity or route completeness
transaction fee metadata is not a complete breakdown of priority fee, Jito tip, protocol/creator fee and realized proceeds
default no-match output may look successful unless callers inspect event arrays and parser status
validation: pin exact parser revision and protocol IDs; compare successful and failed transactions to official SDK/on-chain fixtures
